title: Polynomial diagonal dual base change and graph tensor cancellation
statement:
Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented map of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Fix a surjection $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Distinguish copies $A_1,A_2$ of $A$, put $S=A_1\otimes_RP=A_1[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $B=A_1\otimes_RA_2$, and let $q:S\twoheadrightarrow B$ be the induced surjection. Let $\mu:B\to A$ be multiplication and $e=\mu q:S\to A$. Work in ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For a ring map $f$, let $C_f$ denote derived coinduction with precomposition action [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Put $D=C_{P\to A_2}(P[0])\in D(A_2)$ and $E=C_q(S[0])\in D(B)$. Then $P,S$ are Noetherian, $P\to S$ and both coprojections $A_i\to B$ are flat, and $B[0]$ and the restriction of $E$ are perfect over $S$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. There is an isomorphism
$$E\cong B\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbf L}D\quad\text{in }D(B).$$
The canonical $S$-linear bidual map $B\to R\operatorname{Hom}_S(E,S)$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. Moreover there is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Res}_q(A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E)\cong\operatorname{Res}_eD\quad\text{in }D(S),$$
where $A$ has its multiplication $B$-action on the left, and $D$ is viewed as an $A$-object via $A_2=A$ on the right. In particular, for $s=a\otimes p\in S$ the action on the right is multiplication by $a\bar p=e(s)$; the base change uses the second coprojection.

source.place: Agent polynomial base-change and graph-action argument: Tags 068X (lemma-perfect-over-polynomial-ring), 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), 08YU (lemma-double-base-change); coinduction enhancement supplied by the algebraic-shriek-calculus flat-base-change comparison. Former steps 2, 3 and 6 of lem-trf-polynomial-diagonal-rhom-reduction; complete retained argument in report.md.

proof.text: The monomial generators give finite-type presentations of $P$ over $R$, $S=A_1[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ over $A_1$, and $B$, a quotient of $S$, over $A_1$. Thus the finite-type Noetherian permanence lemma gives that $P,S,B$ are Noetherian. For an injection $U\to V$ of $P$-modules, the identification $U\otimes_PS=U\otimes_RA_1$ (and similarly for $V$) identifies its scalar extension with an injection by flat tensor exactness for $A_1/R$. Hence $P\to S$ is flat. For an injection of $A_1$-modules use $U\otimes_{A_1}B=U\otimes_RA_2$ and flatness of $A_2/R$; interchanging the copies proves flatness of the second coprojection as well. Explicitly, $U\otimes_PS\to U\otimes_RA_1$ sends $u\otimes(a\otimes p)$ to $pu\otimes a$, with inverse $u\otimes a\mapsto u\otimes(a\otimes1)$; $U\otimes_{A_1}B\to U\otimes_RA_2$ sends $u\otimes(a\otimes b)$ to $au\otimes b$, with inverse $u\otimes b\mapsto u\otimes(1\otimes b)$; the case of the second coprojection is symmetric.

source.place: Tags 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), 00HD (lemma-flat); explicit balanced-tensor identification for base change

proof.text: Apply the flat polynomial quotient perfectness lemma first to $R\to A_2$ with presentation $P\twoheadrightarrow A_2$. Finite presentation supplies finite type, and both rings are Noetherian by hypothesis. It gives that $A_2[0]$ is perfect over $P$. Apply the same lemma to $A_1\to B$ with presentation $S=A_1[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow B$: step 1 supplies Noetherianity, flatness and finite type. This gives that $B[0]$ is perfect over $S$.

By the definition of coinduction, the restriction of $E=C_q(S[0])$ is $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,S)$. The closed symmetric monoidal structure on the ordinary module derived category is furnished by the one-object ringed-site instance of the cited monoidal lemma (this site is small); in particular it is braided. Apply perfect-complex biduality over $S$ to the perfect object $B[0]$ from step 2, using a localization universe equal to the coefficient universe as in that lemma. Its dual, namely the restriction of $E$, is perfect, and its canonical evaluation is precisely $B\to R\operatorname{Hom}_S(E,S)$, so that map is an isomorphism. These are assertions in $D(S)$.

source.place: Tag 07VI (lemma-dual-perfect-complex), applied to B over S

proof.text: There is a canonical algebra identification $A_2\otimes_PS\cong B$: $b\otimes(a\otimes p)\mapsto a\otimes b\bar p$, with inverse $a\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes(a\otimes1)$. Apply coinduction flat quotient base change to $P\twoheadrightarrow A_2$, the flat map $P\to S$ of step 1, and $M=P[0]$. Its hypotheses hold: $P$ is Noetherian and $P[0]\in D^+(P)$. The resulting isomorphism is $D\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbf L}B\cong C_q(S[0])=E$ in $D(B)$, where the structure map $A_2\to B$ is $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Write its left side as $B\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbf L}D$: the degree-zero algebra factor contributes no sign. Thus this comparison retains the full $B$-action; it is not just an underlying $S$-linear isomorphism.

Choose a K-flat complex $Q$ of flat $A_2$-modules representing $D$. The cited resolution lemma supplies it; change of rings makes $B\otimes_{A_2}Q$ a K-flat complex of flat $B$-modules. The derived tensor computation therefore represents $B\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbf L}D$ by this complex, and represents $A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}(B\otimes_{A_2}^{\mathbf L}D)$ by $A\otimes_B(B\otimes_{A_2}Q)$, computing in the K-flat factor using the cited derived symmetry; its sign is trivial on the degree-zero ring factor. The balanced chain isomorphism $a\otimes(b\otimes z)\mapsto a\mu(b)\otimes z$, with inverse $a\otimes z\mapsto a\otimes(1\otimes z)$, identifies this with $A\otimes_{A_2}Q$. Since the composite $A_2\to B\xrightarrow{\mu}A$ is the specified identification $A_2=A$, multiplication identifies the last complex with $Q$. The formulas respect differentials since the ring factors are in degree zero. Combining with step 4 gives the required cancellation after restriction along $q$.

source.place: Tag 08YU (lemma-double-base-change), explicit K-flat proof; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat)

proof.text: On the cancellation model, $s=a_1\otimes p\in S$ acts on the $A$ factor through $\mu q(s)=a_1\bar p$. The chain map in step 5 sends $a\otimes(b\otimes z)$ to $a\mu(b)z$, so sends $s$ times this tensor to $(a_1\bar p)a\mu(b)z$. This is exactly the action on $Q$ after restriction along $e$. Consequently the cancellation is $S$-linear and yields $\operatorname{Res}_q(A\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}E)\cong\operatorname{Res}_eD$ in $D(S)$. In particular it uses the second coprojection $A_2\to B$, as asserted.
